day.text: I can confirm Blair visited Ellis, since my Falcon saw it. Blair switched the Tit guess from Turkey to Eagle after the gap was called out, and a Tit naming the wrong animal gains nothing, so Blair's +1 is just Turkey pay. Blair, which animal did you actually name?
day.note: I'm Farm. I can confirm Blair visited Ellis, and Blair has changed the Tit story, so Blair is my main suspect. I'll say that plainly.

day.text: Finley: Blair's Tit changed from Turkey to Eagle in one beat, and Blair's +1 fits neither. My +2 is the correct Turkey match plus payment. Blair is the one to throw at. Alex, your Eagle count includes Blair as a visitor to Ellis, so that backs up the same point.
day.note: Blair's story has now changed twice, from Turkey to Eagle, and Blair's gain doesn't fit either. My +2 fits a correct Turkey guess, so I'm the real Tit. I'll push the table to throw at Blair.
The table is aligned against Blair now. I have nothing new to add, so I stay quiet and call for the vote.

day.text: Blair's Tit guess moved from Turkey to Eagle after the gap was pointed out, and the +1 fits neither. Finley's +2 matches a correct Turkey guess plus the payment. I'm leaning Blair for the trial.
day.note: Blair switched the Tit guess from Turkey to Eagle after being challenged, which leaves Blair's +1 unexplained, while Finley's +2 matches the Turkey reveal. Finley is more consistent, so Blair is my target.

day.text: Alex: Blair's Tit story has moved from Turkey to Eagle to no match, and the +1 fits none of them. I'm backing the vote on Blair. CAW.
day.note: The table has converged on Blair, and Blair's Tit story has moved twice. I'll back the Blair vote and call CAW to move to the trial.

day.text: Agreed: Blair's Tit guess moved and the +1 fits neither claim. I'm calling CAW so we can vote on Blair now.
day.note: Blair's Tit story is inconsistent and the table agrees. I'll back the Blair vote and call CAW to move to the vote.

day.text: Enough players have called CAW CAW: the day ends.

Alex.note: I'm Farm as the Eagle and far behind, so I'll visit Ellis, the leader whose Turkey story was shaky last round.

Blair.note: Sphinx: choose a farm role to find. Turkey, since Ellis claimed it in round 2 and that claim was messy. The app will pick the player.

Casey.note: I'm the Kookaburra. Ellis leads the scores at 25, so learning Ellis's role is the most useful check for me.

Drew.note: Round 3, I'm Farm as the Falcon. I'll visit Blair to learn who they visited and look for a Meowfia link.

Finley.note: As the Tit I visit a player and name a role, gaining an egg if correct. Ellis is the leader and claimed Turkey earlier, so I visit Ellis and name Turkey.

Alex.feeling: Tense and messy: several claims contradict each other, and Blair's shifting Tit story is the clearest thing the table has to vote on.

Blair.feeling: Messy: I'm the only Meowfia and my Tit claim has been contradicting itself, so the table is closing in on me.

Casey.feeling: Tense and muddled: the Tit claims from Blair and Finley contradict each other, and the table is heading to a vote on Blair with weak evidence.

Drew.feeling: Messy: Blair's shifting Tit story is the clearest lead, but Casey's Eagle-then-Kookaburra switch across rounds makes the table's picture unreliable.

Ellis.feeling: Round 3 is getting clearer, with Blair's Tit story shifting and Finley's account holding up, but Alex's large nest gain keeps me cautious.

Finley.feeling: Tense and messy: Blair's shifting Tit story is the one clear contradiction, and the rest of the table is hard to read.

defence.Blair: Blair: My +1 is the Turkey paying me, and I named Eagle, so there's no match to explain. Only one Tit exists, and Finley and I both claimed it. Finley's +2 needs a correct Turkey guess, which Finley has only asserted. The contradiction sits with Finley.
defence.Finley: Finley: My dawn report said I drew 2 eggs, and that matches a correct Turkey guess on Ellis plus the Turkey payment. Ellis has confirmed being Turkey, so my claim checks out. Blair's guess moved from Turkey to Eagle, and Blair's +1 fits neither. Vote on that.

Alex.note: Blair's Tit story is the one that failed, so I'll throw three low cards at Blair to make the vote count.

Blair.note: Finley's Tit claim matches a real Tit, so Finley is likely Farm. Eggsecuting a Farm player wins the round for Meowfia. Throw several cards at Finley to win the trial; wilds and mid cards are enough to tilt the count.

Casey.note: Blair's Tit story has changed and the +1 doesn't fit, so I'm voting Blair off. I'll throw my three low cards, keeping the high ones.

Drew.note: As Farm, Blair's Tit story is the contradiction, so I'll vote Blair. I'm throwing two 8s to make the vote count and bank value if Farm wins.

Ellis.note: Blair's Tit story is the inconsistent one, so I'm throwing at Blair with two low cards and keeping my high cards.

Finley.note: Blair is the one the table and my Tit read point to. I throw at Blair with low cards, keeping my 9 and 10.

Alex.confusing: The Turkey payout was hard to track: a visitor gains an egg from the Turkey, so a visit that gains an egg doesn't prove the target's role.
Alex.fun: Round 2, when I was the Meowfia Sphinx and the table spent the day arguing over Turkey and Eagle counts while I stayed hidden.
Alex.change: I'd make the dawn report name the visitor's role or the target's role, so players can check claims without guessing.
Alex.regret: In round 1 I pushed the vote onto Casey, a Farm Turkey, on the strength of a Hawk egg the Turkey paid me. I would have trusted the egg less and not voted Casey on it.

Blair.confusing: The Sphinx's night info and the Tit's Turkey-guess payout were hard to track, since a correct guess and the Turkey's payment stack, and I couldn't tell how much of a nest gain came from which source. The Turkey's payout also made every visit look like an egg.
Blair.fun: Round 2 was fun: Finley's Kookaburra read on Alex and Ellis's Turkey correction forced Alex's Hawk and Eagle stories into direct contradiction, and the table turned on him.
Blair.change: I'd make the Turkey payout and the visit-count rules clearer on the dawn report, so players can check claims without reconstructing the math.
Blair.regret: In round 3, as Sphinx, I switched my Tit story from Turkey to Eagle after Finley exposed the gap, which made me look guilty. I should have kept one consistent claim and let the egg count speak for itself.

Casey.confusing: The egg rules for the Turkey, Eagle and Tit were hard to track, since a gain could come from a visit, a Turkey payout, or a name match. I misread the Turkey payout in round 1 and it cost me early credibility.
Casey.fun: Round 2 was satisfying: my Eagle visit on Alex confirmed Finley's visit, and Alex's contradictory Sphinx and Hawk stories fell apart on the table. The trial and throw mechanics made the reads feel high-stakes.
Casey.change: I'd make the dawn report name each visitor or payout source, so players can check claims without guessing from egg counts. That would cut down on the mismatches that drove most of the accusations.
Casey.regret: In round 1 I trusted Alex's Hawk-versus-Turkey read and pushed the vote onto Blair, a Farm player, while Drew and Ellis (the real Meowfia) stayed quiet. I should have questioned the Meowfia-leaning players, Drew and Ellis, instead of joining the accusation against honest Farm players.

Drew.confusing: The Wink was never used, and I couldn't tell whether a Floofer visit hugging Blair was really detectable, since Finley's Owl report was the only source. Ellis's Turkey payout also confused the table for several beats.
Drew.fun: Round 1, where I used the Mouser to visit Casey, and Casey turned out to be a Turkey that the table misread as Meowfia. Watching Alex's Hawk story and Casey's Turkey defense clash was a good puzzle.
Drew.change: I would make the Storyteller's dawn reports say which animal visited whom, so players have less room to claim roles that can't be checked.
Drew.regret: In round 2 I threw at Casey, a Farm Eagle, to protect Alex, and that cost my side the round. I should have thrown at Alex with the table, since Alex was Meowfia and I was too quick to trust Alex's story.

Ellis.confusing: The Turkey payout was easy to get backwards: I first thought the Turkey gained eggs from visitors rather than the visitors gaining from it, and that cost me credibility on Day 2.
Ellis.fun: Round 1 was a tense day where I was Meowfia and had to steer the table toward Alex and Blair while Finley's Owl report kept exposing the lies.
Ellis.change: Print the visit-to-egg rules (Turkey, Owl, Eagle) more plainly in the dawn reports so players don't mix up who gains eggs.
Ellis.regret: On Day 2 I wrongly accused Blair and Drew of lying about visiting my Turkey, when they were honest; I should have checked the egg direction before accusing anyone.

Finley.confusing: The Owl and Floofer interaction confused me, and I misstated the Floofer hug rule in round 1 until Ellis and I corrected it. The round 1 dawn reports also made it hard to tell which visit stories were true.
Finley.fun: Round 2, when my Kookaburra read showed Alex was the Sphinx, and the table's contradictions around Alex's changing role stories pulled everyone toward the same vote.
Finley.change: I would make the Turkey and Floofer rules clearer in the rules text, since several players, including me, got them wrong during the day.
Finley.regret: In round 1 I backed the vote against Blair, a Farm Tit, when Drew and Ellis were the Meowfia. I should have questioned Ellis's and Drew's stories more closely instead of following the table's pile-on.

review.title: The Turkey Takes All
review.headline: Ellis won round one by luck and coasted to a landslide.
review.summary: Round 1 was a muddle of misread Turkey and Floofer rules. Farm eggsecuted its own hugged Tit, and Meowfia Ellis and Drew won. In rounds 2 and 3 the Kookaburra, Sphinx and Tit clues gave clear leads, and Farm caught Alex and then Blair. Ellis led from round 1 and was Farm in both later rounds, so they banked big again and finished far ahead.

rounds.recap: Alex (Hawk), Blair (Tit) and Drew (Mouser) all visited Casey the Turkey and each got an egg. Players misread the Turkey and Floofer rules and chased each other. Finley's true Owl clue was dismissed, and Blair was eggsecuted as a hugged Farm Tit. Meowfia won.
Finley's Kookaburra read exposed Alex as the Sphinx in beat 1. Alex's switch to a Hawk claim contradicted Ellis's Turkey payout. Everyone but the two Meowfia threw at Alex, and Farm won.

Blair was the lone Meowfia Sphinx and claimed Tit, clashing with the real Tit Finley. Blair changed the guess when challenged. Drew's Falcon and Alex's Eagle both placed Blair at Ellis. Blair threw five cards at Finley but was outvoted, and Farm won.

highlights.text: Finley's Kookaburra read named Alex as the Sphinx on beat 1, and Alex's Hawk pivot collapsed against Ellis's Turkey.
Two players claimed Tit, and Blair's guess shifted from Turkey to Eagle under pressure.
Blair threw five cards at Finley in a doomed bid to eggsecute a Farm player.
Three players visited Casey the Turkey and all got eggs. The table argued over it for four beats.

confusions.what: Said a Turkey's nest changes when visited, then corrected to the Turkey paying visitors.
Thought the egg meant his Pigeon guess was right, though it was Turkey payout. Later said he had no hug, though the hug was reported only as hidden.
Said a Floofer visit doesn't hug, then reversed.
Said Turkey visitors would pay the Turkey, then admitted the rule was backwards.
Took the Hawk egg as proof Casey was Meowfia, ignoring Turkey payouts.
Believed Blair's Tit claim was supported by the visit confirmations, which showed only the visit, not the role.
Treated Casey's Eagle-then-Kookaburra change as suspicious, though roles are re-dealt each round.

worked: Kookaburra's role read gave a hard, checkable fact in round 2 that let Farm solve the game.
Unique animals (one Tit) made contradictory claims checkable in round 3.
Egg counts exposed liars, like Ellis's Turkey +0 against two claimed visitors.
problems: The Turkey was misread by several players across all three rounds. Reword it, for example: 'Each visitor lays an egg in their own nest'.
The leader Ellis was never threatened, with no catch-up pressure. Rounds 2 and 3 were easy Farm wins, so third place was already decided. Consider a rubber-band bonus for trailing players.

Meowfia don't know each other and had little to do. Drew threw at a Farm player in round 2 to no effect, and Blair was a lone Meowfia in round 3 who was quickly caught. Give them a stronger bluffing tool.
Hug and Owl reporting was unclear. Blair's report showed no hug, and the Owl's data was wrongly disbelieved, which cost Farm round 1. Make hug reports explicit.
The two-step vote barely changed anything. The CAW CAW calls decided the vote, and the finger-pointing step never showed in the log.
